stories.headline: Jensen Huang admits affair as Nvidia board opens spy probe
stories.dek: Nvidia's CEO apologized to staff for infidelity after reports tied him to a suspected Chinese agent; independent directors will investigate.
stories.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to being unfaithful to his wife in a letter to staff. Nvidia's board has opened an independent investigation after reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Tom's Hardware reports that the affair was with a woman US intelligence believes is a Chinese spy. The board said late Sunday that it has no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, and that it remains confident in Huang and his leadership team.

"I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did," Huang wrote. Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 41 years. The letter does not name the other woman. On the security concerns, he said he supports the investigation and "will cooperate fully."

The board said a committee of independent directors, assisted by outside counsel, will oversee the probe and "examine all available information." It added that US national and economic security is "paramount" to Nvidia and its shareholders.

The first reports surfaced Friday. According to Tom's Hardware, US intelligence agencies believe Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed. She was allegedly recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to gather information and help Chinese companies obtain restricted AI GPUs. Megaspeed has been accused of smuggling $2 billion worth of AI chips into China through its subsidiary Speedmatrix. The alleged intelligence operation has not been independently confirmed. Nvidia earlier rejected suggestions of improper dealings, saying Huang meets thousands of customers and those interactions do not involve sensitive information. Chinese officials have called the espionage allegations unfounded.

The case lands on a CEO who has openly opposed limits on AI GPU sales to China. Huang recently called the "China hawk" label "a badge of shame," drawing criticism from administration figures and other tech executives, including Palantir's CEO.

What happens next is unclear. Tom's Hardware points to Intel's Brian Krzanich, who resigned in 2018 after an internal investigation found a relationship that broke company policy. Nvidia's board has said only that it will provide further updates as appropriate.
key_points: Huang admitted infidelity in a letter to Nvidia staff
Independent directors and outside counsel will lead the board's investigation
Board sees no sign secrets or national security were compromised
Alleged spy is a former executive at chip-smuggling suspect Megaspeed
stories.why_it_matters: Nvidia's CEO is the industry's loudest voice against China chip export limits, so a spy probe could shape GPU export policy and the company's leadership stability.

stories.headline: Goldman Sachs pulls Claude Code from its bankers and traders
stories.dek: New internal guidance limits AI coding agents to the bank's roughly 12,000 engineers, months after its CIO praised trader-built tools.
stories.body:
Goldman Sachs has restricted Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub to its engineers, cutting off most traders and bankers, Bloomberg News reports. Internal guidance updated in October followed a review of productivity and risk concerns. Strats, who span trading, quant research and engineering, keep access. Goldman's in-house AI assistant remains available firmwide.

Some traders are frustrated, according to Bloomberg. They had used the tools to monitor client flows, model market moves and positions, and build presentation material. As recently as July, CIO Marco Argenti was promoting "vibe coding" by non-technical staff.

The move comes as Goldman and Morgan Stanley lead underwriting on Anthropic's IPO, per its October 26 S-1 filing. Goldman also removed Claude for Hong Kong bankers in April, citing contract terms. The Hacker News thread drew 691 points and 384 comments.
key_points: Goldman's October guidance limits Claude Code and GitHub to engineers, about 12,000 of roughly 47,000 staff, Bloomberg reports.
Traders had used the tools to track client flows and model positions; strats keep access.
Goldman is a lead underwriter on Anthropic's IPO, according to the S-1 filed October 26.

sources.title: Two Chinese companies cleared to buy banned Nvidia AI chips have empty offices and unknown addresses

stories.headline: Chinese firms cleared for Nvidia H200 chips have empty offices
stories.dek: A New York Times investigation links New Matrix and Maginfra to US-sanctioned firms, raising doubts about how export licenses are vetted.
stories.body:
Two Chinese companies approved by the US to buy Nvidia H200 AI chips appear to operate from empty offices, according to a New York Times investigation reported by Tom's Hardware. The offices of New Matrix and Maginfra held only some furniture. People working nearby said they had never heard of the firms or seen anyone there.

Both have ties to sanctioned companies. New Matrix founder Li Bin and two other primary owners are connected to Wise Road, a private equity firm sanctioned for helping Beijing acquire sensitive chip technology. Maginfra is suspected of links to Inspur, blacklisted since 2023 for supporting China's military. Neither is the final user. Both are supposed to build AI servers for customers who remain unknown.

Around two dozen firms have won approval since President Trump reversed his export ban in exchange for a 25 percent cut of sales. "I have a ton of concerns that neither the Commerce Department or Nvidia is doing the due diligence needed," former National Security Council China director Liza Tobin told the Times.
key_points: New Matrix and Maginfra, approved to buy Nvidia H200 chips, appear to have empty offices, the New York Times reports.
New Matrix's owners are tied to sanctioned Wise Road; Maginfra is suspected of links to blacklisted Inspur.
Around two dozen Chinese firms have received H200 licenses since the US reversed its ban for a 25 percent cut of sales.

sources.title: PC's with 64GB of RAM plummet 18% as memory prices soar

stories.headline: CPU-Z data shows 64GB RAM systems down 18 percent as prices climb
stories.dek: Buyers are shifting to 16GB and 24GB kits and sticking with DDR4 as AI demand pushes memory prices higher, Tom's Hardware reports.
stories.body:
PCs with 64GB of RAM fell 18 percent year over year in CPU-Z's active user base, while 32GB setups slipped 2.5 percent, Tom's Hardware reports. It is the first noticeable decline in higher-capacity configurations the CPU-Z developer has recorded. Tom's Hardware blames DDR4 and DDR5 prices driven up by the AI rush for DRAM supply.

Smaller kits are gaining. 16GB configurations rebounded 12.9 percent, 8GB grew 5.5 percent and 24GB rose 19.7 percent. 32GB still leads with a 37.2 percent share, ahead of 16GB at 33 percent. 64GB sits at 7.3 percent.

DDR4 grew 6 percent to a 54.5 percent share, while DDR5 fell 2.9 percent to 32.9 percent. Older Zen 3 chips such as the Ryzen 5 5500 are climbing too. The figures reflect systems running CPU-Z, not retail sales.
key_points: 64GB configurations fell 18 percent and 32GB fell 2.5 percent year over year in CPU-Z's user base.
16GB rose 12.9 percent, 8GB 5.5 percent and 24GB 19.7 percent as buyers trade down.
DDR4 grew 6 percent to 54.5 percent share; DDR5 fell 2.9 percent to 32.9 percent.

sources.name: BleepingComputer
sources.title: Iris Ohyama data cloud breach exposes info of 7.7 million customers

stories.headline: Iris Ohyama breach may expose data of 7.7 million shoppers
stories.dek: Attackers accessed a third-party cloud service behind the Iris Plaza store, putting names, addresses, birth dates and encrypted passwords at risk.
stories.body:
Japanese household goods maker Iris Ohyama says personal data of about 7.7 million people may have been exposed after unauthorized access to an external cloud service used by its Iris Plaza online store, BleepingComputer reports. Those affected include up to 5.8 million current and former registered members and 1.9 million non-members.

The exposed data may include full names, physical addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, gender, dates of birth and account passwords. The company says active members' passwords are stored encrypted, without naming the scheme, and that no credit card data was kept in the affected service.

Iris Ohyama suspended Iris Plaza and related systems on October 28 and notified police and Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission on October 29. As of November 5, it had no reports of misuse. A spokesperson told BleepingComputer the attacker has not made contact and remains unidentified.
key_points: About 7.7 million people affected: up to 5.8 million current and former members and 1.9 million non-members.
Names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, birth dates and encrypted passwords may be exposed; no credit card data was stored there.
Iris Plaza has been suspended since October 28; no misuse reported as of November 5.

featured.headline: Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade hits a record low: Strong Buy
featured.body:
Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade, a single-player action RPG in the JRPG mold, costs €7.19 at the Epic Game Store. That is 82 percent off its regular €39.99 and the lowest price ever recorded for the game. The reviews support the cut: Very Positive on Steam and a Metascore of 86, the highest of any game in today's deals.

The offer runs until November 16 at 17:00 CET, so there is a full week to decide. At less than a fifth of the usual price, a top-rated game at its all-time low rates a Strong Buy. It suits players who like story-driven action RPGs and have not yet played it.

featured.headline: Streets of Rogue falls to €1.94, its lowest ever: Strong Buy
featured.body:
Streets of Rogue, an action roguelike with pixel graphics, RPG elements and multiplayer, costs €1.94 at Fanatical. That is 90 percent off its regular €19.50 and the lowest price on record. Steam users rate it Overwhelmingly Positive, the top score Steam gives.

The deal ends November 17 at 00:59 CET. A record-low price, a 90 percent cut and one of the best Steam ratings in today's list earn it a Strong Buy. It is the pick for roguelike fans, and the multiplayer tag makes it a candidate for playing with friends as well as alone.
